chromy: Chromy's Sequential Sampling with Probability Minimum Replacement

Source: R/chromy-package.R
chromy-package.Rd

Selection of survey samples by Chromy's method of sequential random sampling with probability minimum replacement, the procedure behind 'PROC SURVEYSELECT' 'METHOD=PPS_SEQ': each unit's realised number of selections differs from its expected number by less than one, and the sample size is always exact. With it, the apparatus the method is used with in practice: hierarchical serpentine sorting of the frame for implicit stratification; a maximal size measure over several auxiliary variables; the allocation that equalises anticipated coefficients of variation across variables; expected hits with certainty units resolved by iteration or, under minimum replacement, units selected more than once; and the multiplicity estimator with the successive-difference variance. The computational engine is the Rust crate 'chromy-core'. The methods follow Chromy (1979) and Chauvet and Le Gleut (2021) doi:10.48550/arXiv.1912.10896 for the selection, and Folsom, Potter and Williams (1987) for the composite size measure.

Selection of survey samples by Chromy's (1979) method of sequential random sampling: chromy_sample() draws the sample, over a frame listed by serpentine_order(), with a size from mpps_size() and eqcv_allocation() or from a single column, expected hits from expected_hits(), and totals estimated by estimate_total(). The numerical engine is the Rust crate chromy-core; all randomness comes from R's own generator, so set.seed() makes a selection exactly reproducible.
